mechanism_narrative: A decline in the federal funds rate over the past month signals an active monetary easing policy, which reduces the risk-free rate and increases the present value of future equity cash flows, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months when FEDFUNDS declines, or the Rank IC falls below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in the unemployment rate above 3.7% signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate earnings growth, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when UNRATE exceeds 3.7, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both residential construction (HOUST) and consumer spending (RSAFS) signals a broad-based weakening in the demand for goods and services, which reduces corporate revenue growth expectations and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when both HOUST < 1500 and RSAFS < 500000, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: During periods of declining industrial production (INDPRO < 108.0), manufacturing output contraction reduces corporate profit margins and future earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when INDPRO < 108.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in consumer spending (RSAFS) over the past month signals strong aggregate demand, which supports corporate revenue growth and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 60% of the months when RSAFS increases, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the federal funds rate above 2.0% within the past month signals an aggressive monetary tightening cycle, which increases discount rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: The 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when FEDFUNDS > 2.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both non-farm payrolls (PAYEMS) and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market contraction due to reduced hiring, which lowers consumer spending and corporate earnings, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: The 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when PAYEMS < 152000 and UNRATE < 3.4, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.

mechanism_narrative: In periods of high inflation (CPIAUCSL > 260.0), central banks are likely to tighten monetary policy, which increases interest rates and reduces equity valuations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: The 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the months when CPIAUCSL > 260.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over a rolling 3-year window.
